t0z4fa: «Cualquiera» stands alone when it works as a pronoun and drops the «a» before a noun: «cualquier bolsa», «cualquier persona». The plural, «cualesquiera», is formal and rare. In conversation people prefer «el que», «quien» or «donde» + subjunctive, with the same meaning: «El que llegue primero abre el depósito», «Plantamos donde diga el guardaparques».

1x1crn0: Four tonnes and a borrowed van
834cus: Chronicle published in the local section of a Mar del Plata newspaper at the end of the summer season. The people and the organization are fictitious.
thr359: On Sunday, while the last tourists were loading their suitcases into their cars, some forty volunteers met at the headquarters of the Costa Limpia network, in the harbour district, to take stock of the season. Its coordinator, Graciela Ibarra, a biologist whose campaigns began six years ago with just five friends, opened the meeting with a figure: between December and March, the network removed almost four tonnes of waste from the beaches, quite a lot more than anyone had calculated.
mcuzmx: Ibarra explained that half of what was collected was cigarette butts and plastic bottle caps, which, she said, «shows that the problem isn't just the big dumps, but the small gestures of every day». She clarified that, although the figure may look like a success, it isn't entirely one: «If we collect so much, it's because a lot was thrown away». However much the network grows, she insisted, without a change of habits the work has no end.
1xr19pl: It wasn't all figures. The head lifeguard of the southern area, Ramón Etcheverry, reminded the volunteers that nobody was to go into the water to collect waste, whatever happened. He said that in February a young man had gone in with a red flag to rescue a fishing net and that the rip current nearly carried him away. «Anyone who sees something floating, let a lifeguard know», he asked. «That's what we're here for».
tpampp: Then it was time for plans. Ibarra proposed that next year the network also work on the southern beaches, where access is harder and rubbish piles up for weeks without anyone removing it. To do that, she said, a van is needed and someone to drive it. She asked if there was anyone present with a professional licence, which was followed by an awkward silence. Two days later, as the coordinator herself confirmed to this newspaper, a volunteer who hadn't been able to attend offered to drive, and a harbour shopkeeper, whose name he preferred not to give, lent the van.
jqgzu6: There were disagreements too. Some volunteers complained that the shift started at seven in the morning. Ibarra replied that, although she understood the tiredness, it was the only time when the tide was low and the beach empty, so she had no intention of changing it. She did promise, however, that as soon as she had the calendar she would send it so that each volunteer could choose their days in advance.
iulyb8: At the end, the coordinator thanked everyone as if they had saved the whole ocean, and more than one person was moved. Wherever you look, this network's work is small compared with the size of the problem. But anyone who has walked along Varese beach this morning, without a single cigarette butt in sight, knows that the difference exists.
